title: Drawing-to-Quote Engine
note: say = what the narrator reads and what the captions show. tts = pronunciation hint for the scratch voice only.

lines.say: One line on this plan reads 12,170.
lines.tts: One line on this plan reads twelve thousand, one hundred and seventy.

lines.say: It's the diagonal, not the wall.
Misread it, and that plot's £157 short.
lines.tts: Misread it, and that plot's a hundred and fifty-seven pounds short.

lines.say: Drop in the whole pack. It finds the three pages that matter,
and proposes every measurement, right beside the line it came from.
So when it reads 12.17, the estimator sees the diagonal, and puts 13.
lines.tts: So when it reads twelve point one seven, the estimator sees the diagonal, and puts thirteen.

lines.say: Everything follows. The perimeter. The lifts. The price.
If the drawing doesn't say, it leaves the field empty, and won't price until someone fills it.
The rate band stays the estimator's call.
Then every line goes into the estimating system, with the page it came from.
Across a forty-plot phase, that's £6,294 that no longer gets given away.
lines.tts: Across a forty-plot phase, that's six thousand, two hundred and ninety-four pounds that no longer gets given away.

lines.say: The drawings arrive. The quote follows.
